characters.description: The former Hero of Lian, presumed dead since the explosion that ended a secretly staged war, now living in Milten behind the mask of the smith Ifrit and leading the guild Menagerie from Lillia's tavern. He carries the unique Living Forge class and a curse, the Hungering Maw, that forces him to devour magic to survive; his smithy is the sentient Infernal Armory and his hammer, Caldera, an evolved living weapon. As book 5 opens he attends the Adept Proving Grounds only as a spectator, unable to fight for fear of recognition, while two teams he equipped compete.
characters.name: Arwin Tyrr

characters.description: The former Demon Queen, stripped of her old power by the same explosion that felled Arwin, now hiding in Milten as the innkeeper of the monster-themed Devil's Den. She carries the unique Hearthkeeper class, which grows stronger through the guests she feeds and lodges, and her tavern is bonded to her as a powerful familiar. Arwin's partner and a founding member of the Menagerie, she keeps the guild's home base thriving while the tournament proceeds far away, and despises needless killing.
characters.name: Lillia

characters.description: A former street thief of Milten and full member of the Menagerie, carrying the unique Warden class built on restraint and control rather than killing. Guarded and shaped by a hard childhood, she is fiercely loyal to Arwin and a lifelong expert sneak. At the Proving Grounds she serves as his eyes, using an item he made to walk through walls and move unseen while she scouts the competing teams.
characters.name: Reya

characters.description: A scarred, battle-tested warrior and full member of the Menagerie who lost her right arm years ago and now fights with a cursed wooden replacement that augments her strength and hungers for death. Loyal and quietly proud, she competes at the Proving Grounds as the third fighter for the allied guild Phoenix Circle, carrying the private weight of a personal Challenge tied to her lost arm.
characters.name: Olive

characters.description: A centuries-old lich, long known on Arwin's street only as a harmless blue-eyed drunkard before revealing himself as its silent guardian of some seven hundred years and the source of the neighborhood's ghost rumors. Allied to Arwin, he helped forge the core of the Soul Guardian and awaits the new body Arwin promised him. He senses that the world itself is slowly starving.
characters.name: Koyu

characters.description: A dwarven master smith and Arwin's informal mentor, a purist steeped in the dwarves' craft and their long trade in weapons and materials. Gruff but genuinely fond of Arwin, he is one of the few who knows something of the smith's methods, and Arwin turns to him for guidance as he pushes his craft toward ever more ambitious work.
characters.name: Wallace Gentletongue

characters.description: A steady warrior in heavy plate and founding member of the Menagerie, married to the healer Anna. Once a genuine paladin who lost his holy class, he now fights as an ordinary man-at-arms and serves as the guild's tactical mind. Behind the scenes he runs an extensive network of street informants, and his intelligence work repeatedly proves decisive in guarding the guild against threats others cannot see.
characters.name: Rodrick

characters.description: A kind, forthright healer and member of the Menagerie, married to Rodrick. An ordinary healer rather than a battle-mage, her power is limited by her own energy, yet she is the guild's lifeline through its hardest fights. Her guarded past includes a rare command of poisons and a history with the Secret Eye that she keeps closely held.
characters.name: Anna

characters.description: The elderly, archaic-mannered proprietor of a cluttered curiosity shop who secretly deals in cursed items and can sense a person's greed. Her shop can open its doors to almost any location, letting her bypass ordinary travel controls. Eccentric and prone to demanding odd payments, she has attached herself to the Menagerie and its projects, though she operates under rules of her own that she rarely explains.
characters.name: Esmerelda

characters.description: An extremely powerful adventurer once renowned as Kien of the Twin Blades and a former solo champion of the Proving Grounds, whose magic and strength were stolen by his own brother, Hein, through an enchanted dagger. Left powerless, he earned a new class and now fights with a soul-imprinted weapon that is, outwardly, a plain broom. He competes for the Menagerie-backed Thornhelm team alongside Art and Vix, intent on finding and killing Hein, who has entered the tournament wielding his stolen power.
characters.name: Kien

characters.description: Duke Aleric's teenage son and reluctant heir to a declining noble house in Thornhelm. Born with a malformed leg, he cannot fight and walks with a crutch, but he is a formidable strategist who keeps detailed intelligence on people in a deck of illustrated cards. He competes at the Proving Grounds beside his sister Vix and Kien, the family's last hope to win a prize that might cure her, and has become a close ally of the Menagerie.
characters.name: Art

characters.description: Art's sister and the fighting strength of Duke Aleric's house in Thornhelm, an elite but visibly ailing warrior dying of a congenital heart condition with only a few years left. She competes at the Proving Grounds alongside her brother and Kien, staking everything on the tournament's prize as her family's last chance at a cure and at restoring their standing.
characters.name: Vix

characters.description: A bandaged, reserved fighter of the struggling guild Phoenix Circle, wrapped head to foot in cloth and evasive about himself, who partners with the Menagerie for the Proving Grounds. He fights beside Olive and his close companion Maeve, and leaves the impression of being something other than he appears.
characters.name: Elias

characters.description: A tall, masked, mute fighter of Phoenix Circle, introduced as Elias's companion and never far from his side. Armed with daggers and unusually strong, she keeps her true strength deliberately held back and is not human. She fights beside Olive and Elias on the Menagerie-partnered team at the Proving Grounds.
characters.name: Maeve

characters.description: An observer for the Secret Eye, the body that ranks guilds and runs the Proving Grounds. Carried from the Menagerie's earlier dealings, she brought the guild into the tournament and continues to watch its teams and Reya's movements from among the event's staff, weighing the Menagerie as she would any other competitor.
characters.name: Selen

characters.description: Kien's estranged younger brother, competing alone at the Proving Grounds while flanked by two silent cloaked attendants. He carries an enchanted dagger that harms only through bare flesh, the same blade with which he stole his brother's magic and strength, and he keeps his true power hidden. Kien has entered the tournament to find and kill him.
characters.name: Hein

characters.description: An operative of the Setting Sun, the numbered organization tied to the late assassin Twelve. Sleep-loving and reluctant, she is sent by her superior One to scout the Proving Grounds for potential recruits whose classes can be 'sun-set.' Watching from a rented viewing room, she is unsettled by the lethal power of the gear the Menagerie's fighters carry and begins studying the guild in earnest.
characters.name: Eleven

characters.description: A mysterious master smith, treated as the rival dwarven soul-smith the Secret Eye warned Arwin about. His durable soul-forged armor turns up equipping the Starforge team at the Proving Grounds, but his identity, methods, and true purpose remain unknown.
characters.name: Necrohammer

characters.description: A merchant and Arwin's metal supplier, and secretly a vampire. Once a soldier in Lillia's old army, he recognized his former queen and swore himself to her service. Formal and theatrical but quick to violence when crossed, he keeps the smithy stocked and, as the guild's fame and takings surge during the tournament, helps move its growing fortune to safety.
characters.name: Madiv

characters.description: An untrained noble boy of about fifteen, second in line to the wealthy House Blacktongue, whose parents mean to purchase him a powerful class through a paid delve into an expert-tier dungeon. An obsessive researcher who has studied the Menagerie closely, he is odd, humble, and sharp, and he has calmly calculated that he will not survive the delve. He becomes the Menagerie's escort charge.
characters.name: Thane Blacktongue

characters.description: A Dwarven Master Smith, trained by and daughter to the Dwarven Council member Indrana, who arrives in Milten posing as a wandering challenger smith. Her real aim is to discover which dwarf broke dwarven law by teaching a human the craft. Arrogant and certain of her master's near-artifact hammer, she wagers it against Arwin and loses both the bet and the hammer, and is left publicly humiliated.
characters.name: Ida

characters.description: A Councilwoman of the Dwarven Council and Ida's mother, unwilling to believe Arwin could smith at a master's level without stolen dwarven techniques. Overriding her daughter, she sends the warrior Gideon to kill the smith Ifrit, offering Ida's hand in marriage as the reward and treating her daughter as a bargaining chip in her own political ambitions. She acts from a distance through a telepathic stone.
characters.name: Indrana

characters.description: A dwarf warrior of the Dwarven Council serving under Indrana, and Ida's unwanted longtime suitor. Arrogant and boastful, he is clad head to toe in Indrana's high-grade gold-and-silver enchanted armor and wields a huge magical axe he can dismiss and recall to hand. He is sent to Milten to kill the smith Ifrit in exchange for Ida's hand in marriage.
characters.name: Gideon

recaps.ending: Book 5 closes without resolving its two headline setups. The planned infiltration of the Blacktongue party to expose the Adventurer's Guild operative Mask never happens on the page, and the climax pivots entirely to the Dwarven Council. Convinced Arwin stole dwarven techniques, Councilwoman Indrana sends the warrior Gideon to kill him; Arwin's autonomous ivory golem, the Soul Guardian, defeats Gideon publicly, and Lillia captures him with overwhelming shadow magic. Where the major players stand: Arwin is unharmed at his forge, his power decisively displayed through the golem, with his new armor begun but not finished. Lillia has taken command of the aftermath, openly revealed as non-human, and is steering a direct confrontation with the Council. Gideon is captured and doomed, though his armor will be returned. Ida, having refused to call her mother for rescue, is estranged in spirit from Indrana and cooperating inside the Devil's Den. Indrana, off page, is about to be contacted directly. The Menagerie and its allies are all alive and thriving. Open threads carry into a possible book 6: the imminent Lillia-Indrana confrontation and the wider Dwarven Council conflict; the still-unexecuted Blacktongue party and the Mask reckoning; the unfinished armor and Koyu's promised body; the legendary vault still unlocated; Eleven's owed explanation of class-sunsetting; Vix's uncured heart; and the deeper mysteries of the dying world, Arwin's growing Hungering Maw, and the Setting Sun's tie to his and Lillia's summoned past and his charge to find One.
recaps.in_short: Rise of the Living Forge 5 follows Arwin Tyrr, the presumed-dead Hero of Lian, working as the masked smith Ifrit and leading the guild Menagerie. At the Adept Proving Grounds, two teams he equipped fight through the tournament: Phoenix Circle reaches the final and, though defeated, saves the dying undead Elias and stops the power-thief Hein, whom Kien kills; and Thornhelm withdraws to spare Kien from execution. The mysterious rival smith Necrohammer is revealed as Norman, Phoenix Circle's vanished founder, who then tells Arwin the world's secret: it is dying, the Guild manufactures war to feed the Mesh with the deaths of summoned heroes, and he saved Arwin and Lillia to break the cycle. Home in Milten, Arwin allies loosely with the Setting Sun, learns soulmancy from the lich Koyu and the dwarf Wallace, and begins building an armor to house his sentient smithy. He clears an expert dungeon to save the noble boy Thane and win a legendary vault-key. The book ends when the Dwarven Councilwoman Indrana sends the warrior Gideon to kill Ifrit: Arwin's autonomous ivory Soul Guardian golem overpowers him, and Lillia captures him with shadow magic, setting up a direct confrontation with the Dwarven Council that carries into the next book.

recaps.text: Previously, across the earlier books: Arwin Tyrr, the presumed-dead Hero of Lian, survived the explosion that ended a secretly staged war and was cast into the remote city of Milten, reborn with the unique Living Forge crafting class and a curse, the Hungering Maw, that forces him to devour magic to live. Working behind the mask of the smith Ifrit, he built a small guild, the Menagerie, around the tavern of Lillia, the former Demon Queen, likewise stripped of her power and now running the Devil's Den. The guild grew to include the thief-turned-Warden Reya, the fallen paladin Rodrick, the healer Anna, the one-armed warrior Olive, the vampire merchant Madiv, and the curiosity-shop dealer Esmerelda. Arwin rose through the tiers, took up soul-forging, and bonded to a sentient smithy, the Infernal Armory, and an evolved living hammer. He allied with a centuries-old lich, Koyu, who warned that the world itself is slowly starving. The Menagerie destroyed the masked assassin Twelve, drawing the notice of the numbered organization he served, the Setting Sun. Invited to a tournament, the Adept Proving Grounds, the guild outfitted two teams: the struggling Phoenix Circle, whose fighters include Olive, the bandaged and secretive Elias, and the non-human Maeve; and the Thornhelm team of the strategist Art, his dying sister Vix, and Kien, a renowned adventurer whose power was stolen by his brother Hein. Book 4 ended at the tournament's opening ceremony, before a single match, with Hein competing using Kien's stolen strength and the Menagerie under fresh outside observation.

So far this book: the Proving Grounds' group-stage melees begin, and Arwin watches from a spectator balcony with Reya, unable to fight for fear the Secret Eye will recognize the Hero of Lian. He spots a two-person team bearing the Setting Sun's silver insignia - a bald, unarmed monk who knocks opponents' spirits loose and a silent staff-wielder - and sends Reya, carrying an item that lets her walk through walls, to scout the field. Esmerelda works the stands in disguise; using a potion that reads life force, she foresees that a poor competitor's son, Arnold, is fated to die, and asks Arwin to help prevent it. Arwin also studies a trio in flawless obsidian dwarven-forged armor and ties them to the rival smith the Secret Eye warned him about. Olive takes the arena for Phoenix Circle and, in her melee, comes face to face with her old team - Jason, Damien, and Bea, the people tied to the loss of her arm, now richly equipped. Shaken but resolute, she defeats all three alone without her signature ability, severing Bea's arm and walking away with hard-won closure.

Reya scouts the tournament openly, unnerving the Secret Eye's observers, who note she walked clean through a warded wall and ignored a bag of tracked gold left as a test. She locates Arnold, plants false intelligence with a rival spy - that Olive's wooden arm is a weakness to be struck - and finds Esmerelda shadowing her to handle the boy herself. Art's team wins its melee carried by Kien, who fights with overwhelming strength and his broom-shaped weapon while hiding his regained power. Arwin confirms that Kien's brother, Hein, is competing alone, carrying a dagger that harms through bare flesh and resists steel, and arranges to warn Olive and Kien. Esmerelda saves Arnold with a limited, costly boost. The melees end and the first proper team round pits Phoenix Circle against the Carreras Coalition, which fields a trio of Falling Blade assassins. Olive kills all three, her cursed arm surging with bloodlust and briefly seizing control to finish the last on its own. The Menagerie advances, and Olive is unsettled by how little the killing moved her.

A Setting Sun operative, Eleven, watches from a rented room, disturbed by Olive's executions and the near-sentient bloodlust of her arm; she is scouting for recruits whose classes can be 'sun-set.' Starforge, led by the gravity mage Ursa, is revealed as the enemy that has been killing Art's family and trying to seize Thornhelm. When the teams meet, Art demonstrates his true power - he can copy and nullify an opponent's magic, storing it in cards - and strips Ursa of his gravity magic. Kien holds off Starforge's synchronized twins, Lily and Ash, alone at Art's insistence, so the team can prove itself. Cornered by Ursa's soul-armor, Art uses a time-freezing ability to plan an escape, then releases a power sealed inside his sister: Vix unleashes invisible, lethal high-speed strikes that carve through the armor and drives a dagger into Ursa's skull, killing him, at the cost of a spreading corruption Art must reseal. The name of the smith behind Starforge's soul-armor surfaces - Necrohammer - and Thornhelm advances, leaving a second Menagerie-outfitted team with dead aggressors in its wake.

Eleven recognizes that the Menagerie deliberately equipped two teams and privately identifies Vix as a warlock bound to her brother Art, revealing herself to be a warlock too when she fails to recruit Kien. Arwin and Reya puzzle over Necrohammer, an evidently masterful smith whose gear performs poorly in real combat; they conclude he has spread single overpowered pieces across nearly a dozen teams as a reputation play. Meanwhile Esmerelda's intervention for Arnold plays out: she had given the doomed boy a cursed sword with a warning never to draw it. When an enemy knight overpowers Arnold's team and draws the blade himself, the weapon's bound devil turns on him and reduces him to dust, sparing Arnold, who refuses to lean on its stolen power, loses the bout, but survives. The reader learns Esmerelda acts as a 'dealer' who places cursed weapons but cannot choose their wielders. The quarterfinals open, matching Phoenix Circle against Blackguard, the pitch-black-armored team Arwin believes Necrohammer fully outfitted.

Phoenix Circle faces Blackguard in the quarterfinal. Olive fights the honorable Vale and the fire-armored second Blackguard fighter two-on-one; deafened by Vale's shrieking sword, she deliberately defies her own sword-purist Challenge without being punished for it, then unlocks the seal on her Ifrit armor, revealing it to be a soul weapon. Her cursed arm gains a voice and bargains for shared control, and Arwin lends her his living hammer, Caldera, for the single fight. Olive's adaptive armor and Maeve's ability to fully deactivate enemy gear win the match; the defeated Vale entrusts Olive with a hidden plain dagger. Studying it, Arwin finds it is a living weapon forged from human finger-bone, twin to Hein's power-stealing dagger, and pieces together that Necrohammer sacrificed his own fingers to build a counter-weapon meant to destroy Hein's. In private, Necrohammer is revealed at last: he is Norman, Phoenix Circle's vanished dwarf-necromancer founder, long ago cast out by the Dwarven Council. His undead fighter Elias is his first and proudest creation, now dying, and Norman means to shatter the daggers and spend their stolen power to save him.

The counter-dagger reaches Art's team just as the semifinal pits them against Hein. Kien unmasks before his stunned brother and, with Art secretly freezing time and feeding his own energy to buy a single decisive moment, beats Hein down; Vix rips the dagger from Hein's hand and Kien clashes the twin blades together, shattering both. Stripped of his stolen power, Hein formally surrenders to hide behind Kien's hero morality - and Kien kills him anyway, punching through his heart and declaring he is no longer a hero. Facing execution by the Adventurer's Guild for the post-surrender kill, Kien intends to die so Art and Vix can go on; Art instead withdraws Thornhelm from the tournament to save him. When a Guild axeman moves to kill Art, Arwin breaks his cover, hurls Caldera, and reveals himself as Ifrit, while Necrohammer publicly backs a lie that the cursed dagger controlled Kien. The Secret Eye accepts Thornhelm's resignation and closes the matter. In private, Necrohammer - dying and out of time - takes the unconscious Elias and works on him with the black gem set in his palm, calling the undead a 'piece' that needs only finishing touches.

The final pits Phoenix Circle against Setting Sun, who field a hidden third member - a forgettable shadow-mage who has scouted all tournament and now targets Olive's arm, exactly as Reya's false intelligence intended, so a blow that should have ended the fight instead glances off her toughest part. Elias, secretly restored by Necrohammer, at last fights with real power and rings himself out along with the near-invincible monk to remove him. Olive, cornered and offered victory by her cursed arm if she will only kill, refuses and is knocked out instead, holding to who she is. Maeve, hearing that Elias's magical 'song' has fully returned, understands Norman truly cured him rather than merely patching him; she eliminates the enemy mage but is then kicked out of bounds, and Setting Sun wins the tournament. Yet Phoenix Circle achieves every real goal: Elias is safe and no longer dying, Hein is stopped, the assassins who targeted the guild are dead, and the Menagerie's craft is proven. The tournament arc closes with the teams parting in mutual respect.

With the tournament over, Necrohammer arranges a private meeting and tells Arwin the truth about the world. He knows Arwin was summoned from another world, and reveals that whole peoples - the dwarves, demons, and more - were mass-summoned long ago. The world is dying, starved of magical energy, and the Mesh harvests a share of every life and death; the endless war exists to feed it. The Adventurer's Guild summons powerful heroes and demon queens, lets them grow strong, then kills them, because a fully realized high-tier class yields the most energy when its holder dies - and any hero who cared to protect the world was killed to keep the war going. Lillia, too, was summoned from another planet, and neither she nor Arwin ever chose their class. Necrohammer reveals it was he who planted the black gem in Arwin's armor, a device that detonated to strip Arwin's magic and halt the rare 'sunsetting' of his class, saving him and Lillia from the Guild's harvest to break the cycle and buy the world time. He urges Arwin to grow stronger, to seek out the figure called One, and to find a way to save a dying world, then departs.

The Menagerie returns to Milten, where the Devil's Den has thrived on tournament crowds and Lillia's growing Hearthkeeper power. Arwin tells the whole guild everything Necrohammer disclosed. The Setting Sun's Eleven arrives at the tavern, probes the guild about Twelve's death, and - impressed that no one panics - pivots from recruitment to an alliance: rather than absorb the Menagerie, One wants a standing, non-exclusive arrangement in which the guild crafts for and works alongside the Setting Sun, gaining access to its dungeons and, eventually, instruction in sunsetting classes. She leaves behind a dungeon heart as a gift and a show of strength. Thornhelm and Phoenix Circle formally attach themselves to the Menagerie; Elias and Maeve stay on, Elias now permanently made whole by a 'monster core' Necrohammer built from Hein's stolen power. Esmerelda recognizes Vix as a warlock, though the guild sets the matter aside. Arwin resolves to fix Vix's heart, possibly through the dungeon heart or her warlock bond to Art, and returns to the forge intent on building himself a powerful new suit of armor before seeking out One.

Arwin settles back into Milten as the Menagerie grows wealthy and famous. He and Lillia plan an auction house for the city, to be run by Madiv, and the guild runs dungeons to stock the smithy. Working with the Infernal Armory, Arwin conceives his flagship project: not merely a suit of armor but one that can house the sentient Armory itself, letting it leave its building and fight at his side. Koyu appears in person as a lich and reacts with fear to the word 'soulmancy' - the ability Arwin unknowingly gained when he made his Soul Guardian. Koyu explains that soulmancy is the art of enslaving a soul, practiced by history's worst liches, and is horrified until he learns Arwin reached it by a wholly different path: genuinely communing with and contracting the willing souls of his materials. He shares a memory of his ancient master, the greater lich Shade, who forged a soul-bound weapon that once ended a war by destroying everything, including itself, and warns that Arwin's own bow may descend from it. Koyu and the dwarven smith Wallace both agree to mentor Arwin, and the three begin training together toward the armor, Arwin advancing to Adept Two.

Arwin tells the entire Menagerie his full origin, and the guild shares its own secrets until nothing is hidden among them. Melissa brings a job: escort the untrained teenage son of the wealthy House Blacktongue into an expert-tier dungeon so the boy can earn a class, with access to the family's crystal mines as the real prize. The boy, Thane, proves to be an odd, humble, obsessive researcher who has calmly concluded he will die in the delve. Arwin, liking the boy but despising the family, resolves to keep Thane alive and to strip the dungeon bare in spite. With Koyu and Wallace, Arwin forges a disposable prototype of his armor - a thin skeleton and bracelets meant to test housing the Infernal Armory remotely - knowing it will break under strain. He assembles an elite three-fighter party of himself, Olive, and Anna, and at the dungeon's threshold uses a newfound power to offer the classless Thane a mesh 'quest,' declaring the fearful boy reborn as one who will never throw his life away.

Deep in the Blacktongue dungeon, Arwin clears rooms with overwhelming force while shielding Thane, who is forbidden to fight. A first boss falls to a single charged arrow, and an entire room of monsters cowers rather than attack. At the final chamber, a hive-mother - an egg-laying bat-and-worm creature surrounded by hatching young - proves un-flankable because it shares its senses with its brood; Thane cracks the puzzle, and by killing hatchlings to disrupt the link the party creates the opening for Arwin to end it with a full-power strike, remotely summoning the Infernal Armory through his prototype armor for the first time. The prototype breaks exactly as predicted, its job done. The Menagerie claims the dungeon's first clear, far beyond what House Blacktongue expected. Thane, who entered certain he would die, breaks down with relief, then discovers he truly earned a class - 'Combat Archivist,' which lets him learn ever more about an item or monster the longer he studies it. Among the loot is a heavily rusted circlet, so encrusted that its magic reads as nothing at all, which the party keeps to examine later. Arwin sends House Blacktongue his regards.

Back in Milten, Arwin and the Infernal Armory design a second, layered version of the armor around a protected core. The challenger smith who has camped outside for weeks finally forces a confrontation and is revealed as Ida, a Dwarven Master Smith and daughter of the Councilwoman Indrana, sent to discover which dwarf illegally taught Arwin his craft. Arwin wins a wager by devouring her master's hammer with his Hungering Maw, hiding his mentor Wallace and humiliating her, though it deepens the Dwarven Council's interest. Eleven returns and offers a new job: infiltrate a coming-of-age party at House Blacktongue, where the Adventurer's Guild is sending an operative called Mask - the man the Setting Sun believes gave Hein the cursed dagger. Arwin agrees, trading Eleven sanctioned observation of the guild for shared intelligence, and resolves to build the new armor within three days and test it against Mask. Reviewing the dungeon loot, the guild confirms the Legendary Band of the Vault Keeper points to a hidden vault that could solve their material needs - and that the Blacktongues do not yet know what they lost.

As the Menagerie prepares to infiltrate the Blacktongue party, Esmerelda produces a genuine signed invitation, secured by her will-driven shop through Thane, who has begun working for her. Pressed on why she keeps placing cursed items despite promising to stop, Esmerelda reveals her true class: her trade is not goods but people, redistributing dangerous items to suitable wielders and keeping the worst from the undeserving, and the guild concludes she has quietly averted disasters for years. Eleven names her 'the Curse Broker' and confirms the Setting Sun tracks everyone whose class has been sunsetted, of whom the Menagerie now holds several. A crate of extraordinary high-grade materials arrives as commission payment, including a room-temperature liquid metal ideal for the armor's flexible interior and a crimson battle-metal that pulls Arwin into a vision of a bloodied, bodiless battlefield and then refuses to communicate. With Wallace and Koyu, Arwin begins forging the most complex armor he has ever attempted, the three minds linked through the Infernal Armory, the day before the party.

While Arwin, Wallace, and Koyu are deep in forging the new armor, the Blacktongue infiltration never happens. Instead, Ida reports to her mother by telepathic stone that Arwin is 'something else entirely,' not dwarven-trained; refusing to believe it, Indrana sends the warrior Gideon - clad in her own high-grade armor and offered Ida's hand in marriage as reward - to kill Ifrit. At the smithy, Arwin's autonomous protective golem, the hollow ivory Soul Guardian animated by crimson magic, awakens and defends the shop. It out-fights the expert-tier Gideon, survives being beheaded because it is empty inside, and bites chunks from his armor and arm with a hungering shark-toothed maw. Before Gideon can make a final effort, Lillia emerges from the Devil's Den, seizes him with overwhelming shadow magic, and drags him inside. Gideon is captured, defeated, and will not leave alive, though his armor will be returned. Ida, refusing to summon her mother for rescue and effectively defecting in spirit, is brought before Lillia, who reveals her fangs and orders Ida to call Indrana on the stone. The book ends there: Lillia leans in and says the three of them are going to have a talk, the direct Menagerie-versus-Dwarven-Council confrontation set up but unresolved.

characters.description: The leader of the Menagerie and master of the Devil's Den. She uses her reach within the shadows to force the Dwarven Council to stop pursuing Ifrit, then recruits Ida as an insider who can report on the dwarves.
characters.name: Lillia

characters.description: A figure pursued by the Dwarven Council until Lillia forces Indrana to end the hunt and surrender any claim of dwarven authority over him.
characters.name: Ifrit

characters.description: Indrana's daughter and a dwarven smith caught between the Council and the Menagerie. She rejects her mother's authority, accepts Lillia's protection, and agrees to serve as the Menagerie's source within the dwarven order.
characters.name: Ida

characters.description: A powerful figure on the Dwarven Council and Ida's mother. Lillia corners her politically and personally, compelling her to end the dwarven pursuit of Ifrit and transfer her smithing hammer to Ida.
characters.name: Indrana

characters.description: A deceased covert informant who worked against the Adventurers Guild. His efforts and death remain important to Arwin.
characters.name: Blake

characters.description: The Menagerie's Living Forge and one of the makers of a legendary connected suit of armor. Working with Wallace, Koyu, and the Infernal Armory, he completes a body for the awakened forge and gains new choices for his own growth.
characters.name: Arwin

characters.description: An awakened forge allied with Arwin and the Menagerie. It helps create a legendary armor set and identifies the completed armor as its own body.
characters.name: Infernal Armory

characters.description: A master artisan who works beside Arwin, Koyu, and the Infernal Armory. His practical experience and control of the forging process help the group finish the connected armor that becomes the awakened forge's body.
characters.name: Wallace

characters.description: A lich artisan bound to Menagerie Street and a trusted participant in Arwin's forge work. He helps Arwin, Wallace, and the Infernal Armory complete the awakened forge's connected armor body.
characters.name: Koyu

characters.description: An attendant at the Devil's Den who firmly enforces its prohibition on violence. When Vanessa arrives looking for Ifrit, Monica stops the visitor from turning a hostile message into a fight inside Lillia's establishment.
characters.name: Monica

characters.description: A hired fighter affiliated with the Shimmering Shield. She comes to the Devil's Den looking for Ifrit and carries an employer's hostile message, but says she was not sent to kill him.
characters.name: Vanessa

characters.description: The publicly unfavored Blacktongue twin, whose analytical class gives him unusually detailed information about objects. His family places him in a duel against the better-equipped Drake, expecting Thane's defeat to strengthen the favored heir's reputation.
characters.name: Thane Blacktongue

characters.description: Thane's twin and the celebrated heir of House Blacktongue. He arranges a public duel that treats Thane as a family asset and an expendable means of enhancing his own status.
characters.name: Drake Blacktongue

characters.description: A Menagerie intelligence operative with a citywide information network. He interferes with Eleven's surveillance of Vanessa as the warrior approaches the Devil's Den.
characters.name: Rodrick

characters.description: A Menagerie member who joins Rodrick in monitoring Vanessa's approach and takes position to oversee Vanessa's confrontation with Arwin.
characters.name: Anna

characters.description: A potion merchant and logistics specialist chosen for the Menagerie's Blacktongue delegation. Her trade knowledge gives the group a credible commercial presence among nobles, while her portable shop provides transportation and supplies.
characters.name: Esmerelda

characters.description: A Menagerie fighter trusted with the defense of the Devil's Den while the Blacktongue delegation travels. She remains with the combatants assigned to protect the guild's home territory.
characters.name: Olive

characters.description: An observer who monitors the Menagerie's growing strength and the dangers gathering around the Blacktongue party. Lillia's ability to block her surveillance makes her reassess the group.
characters.name: Eleven

characters.description: A Menagerie combatant selected to remain at the Devil's Den and help protect the guild's home territory while the Blacktongue delegation travels.
characters.name: Art

characters.description: A Menagerie combatant who remains with the home force to protect the Devil's Den while the Blacktongue delegation travels.
characters.name: Madiv

characters.description: A Menagerie combatant who remains at the Devil's Den with the force assigned to protect the guild's home territory while the Blacktongue delegation travels.
characters.name: Keen

characters.description: An Adventurers Guild operative carrying a dagger designed to steal magic. He approaches the Blacktongues with a dangerous gift and defends the Guild's methods as necessary, prompting Arwin to confront him before the weapon can reach its intended recipient.
characters.name: Mask

characters.description: A senior Setting Sun representative who has abandoned his former name. He evaluates Arwin for class sunsetting and explains that the mesh is failing and the Adventurers Guild's proposed solution is not the only possible path.
characters.name: Two

characters.description: A Menagerie combatant active in the guild's operations.
characters.name: Vix

characters.description: A Menagerie member who can become translucent and pass through solid walls.
characters.name: Phasing Menagerie member

characters.description: A bloodthirsty devil bound to a cursed obsidian axe. It manifests a shadowy form after Thane interferes with its attempt to claim Vanessa, freezing the others nearby while it confronts him.
characters.name: Thane's weapon-devil

characters.description: A Menagerie fighter who joins Arwin, Olive, and Anna on the expedition to recover a hidden vault.
characters.name: Menagerie vault fighter

characters.description: The Menagerie's newly awakened auction house. Its dungeon-heart mechanism is bound to Madiv, who is intended to serve as its controller and auctioneer, but its behavior remains unknown when it first stirs.
characters.name: Mausoleum

characters.description: A Menagerie associate who remains away training when the guild assigns teams for its vault operation. She is not assigned to either active operation team.
characters.name: Maeve

characters.description: A Menagerie associate who remains away training when the guild assigns teams for its vault operation. He is not assigned to either active operation team.
characters.name: Elias

characters.description: The Devil's Den's newly created armored guardian, a transcendent manifested soul rather than owned equipment. She is conscious, recognizes no master, and chooses to defend the Den while reserving lethal force for situations in which she judges death necessary.
characters.name: Lillia's manifested soul guardian

recaps.ending: By the close, the Menagerie remains intact and has become a serious independent power in Milton. The Dwarven Council formally supports the coming auction, while Rodrick uses knowledge of a rival councilor's hidden son to end that faction's immediate interference. Lillia protects an enlarged living domain after completing her sunsetting, and Arwin continues building an alternative to the Adventurers Guild's magic-harvesting strategy. Koyu returns from sunsetting in a stronger lich form but still expects Arwin and Wallace to craft him a body. Vix survives her heart replacement and remains under Anna's restrictions while the new core stabilizes. Thane retains agency under his private contract with the weapon-devil, though control of its violence remains unfinished. Madiv and the awakened Mausoleum prepare for an auction only days away. The unknown sponsor of the attempted abductions remains unidentified, the Guild and dying mesh remain unresolved, and Maeve departs through a portal to begin her own sunsetting while Elias stays with the group.
recaps.in_short: The Menagerie strengthens its position in Milton through living creations, class sunsetting, and a planned high-value auction. Arwin gives the Infernal Armory a mobile body, uncovers the Adventurers Guild's system for harvesting magic, completes his own sunsetting, and transforms his body into a living forge. Lillia, Rodrick, and Koyu also sunset, while the guild creates an autonomous guardian for the Devil's Den and awakens the Mausoleum for Madiv. Thane leaves House Blacktongue, joins the Menagerie, and binds himself by contract to a violent weapon-devil. A vault raid supplies auction stock and helps secure Dwarven Council backing, though a rival faction attacks. Vix survives the replacement of her failing heart with a soul-forged core, and Rodrick deters the Council rival before the numbered story closes. Afterward, Maeve begins sunsetting as the auction nears and Arwin anticipates renewed Adventurers Guild attention.

recaps.text: Lillia forces Indrana to end the Dwarven Council's pursuit of Ifrit and recruits Ida as an insider, leaving the immediate dwarven threat contained. Meanwhile, Arwin, Wallace, Koyu, and the Infernal Armory complete Gehenna the Dreadhusk, a legendary suit that serves as the awakened forge's mobile body. The Armory gains its own class, while Arwin chooses a soul-linking ability whose aura proves far more frightening than he expects. Vanessa arrives at the Devil's Den with a hostile message for Ifrit. Her attempt to test Arwin ends when her enhanced perception exposes her to his deathly aura and she collapses without him knowingly attacking. Rodrick concludes that Vanessa was sent as part of a setup connected to the Blacktongue gathering. Rather than release her, the Menagerie hires her to serve as a visible disruption while Rodrick gathers information. Arwin, Lillia, Rodrick, Esmerelda, Vanessa, and another guild member then leave Milton for the Blacktongue party, while Olive, Madiv, and the remaining defenders secure the street.

House Blacktongue celebrates Drake as its heir while treating his twin Thane as expendable. Drake engineers a public duel that is meant to elevate him through Thane's defeat, but Arwin supplies Thane with Birthday Poker and Lightfinger. The weapons overcome Drake's equipment and lack of restraint, allowing Thane to win, renounce his house, and join the Menagerie. As Vanessa helps reshape the nobles' view of Thane, Rodrick infiltrates Blacktongue Manor under false identities. Arwin watches for Mask, an Adventurers Guild operative expected to place a magic-stealing dagger with a resentful Blacktongue son. He intercepts Mask and creates a public pretext for a duel. Once Esmerelda signals that the group's preparations are complete, Arwin equips Gehenna. Mask draws on red magic for speed and resistance, but his dagger cannot penetrate the living armor. Arwin defeats him, uses a potion to simulate his death, and removes both the captive and dagger while the party believes Mask died. The Menagerie now possesses a living witness and a weapon tied to the Guild's secret activity.

While the party unfolds, a Blacktongue-paid reconnaissance team enters Menagerie territory in search of an alleged artifact. Olive's defenders capture the intruders and release them with a false lead about an expert dungeon, buying time and directing Blacktongue attention away from the real objective. Rodrick burns selected rooms in Blacktongue Manor to erase evidence of his infiltration, and the delegation returns with Thane, Mask, and the stolen dagger. Under interrogation, Mask reveals that the Adventurers Guild uses its daggers to drain magic and feeds them into a concealed pit beneath the Guild Wall. Arwin decides the Menagerie is not yet strong enough to investigate directly. He instead reports the discovery to Eleven, who takes him to meet Two of Setting Sun. Two explains that class sunsetting can realign accumulated power and says the mesh itself is dying. He also reveals that Blake spent years supplying intelligence from within the staged war before the Guild discovered and killed him. Arwin condemns Setting Sun's role in other deadly intelligence operations, but accepts continued cooperation and proceeds toward a second attempt to sunset his class.

Two prepares Arwin for sunsetting at a ley line, but the expected agony barely affects him, likely because his earlier forced attempt already altered his soul. At Setting Sun's volcanic base, Arwin encounters the mesh directly. It explains that classes ration a dwindling reserve of magic and that completed sunsetting removes their deliberate restrictions. The mesh is willing to tolerate both the Adventurers Guild's harvesting plan and Arwin's alternative until a better path is proven. Arwin completes the process, integrating former achievements and abilities into a freer Living Forge class. He returns stronger and with direct control over future advancement. At the mesh's request, Lillia follows him into Setting Sun's process. Unlike Arwin, she suffers through the ley line, but reaches the necessary internal change and completes her ritual at the volcanic platform. Back in the Devil's Den, Lillia learns that customer satisfaction now creates power she can allocate to tavern improvements. Her handmade magical food and drink can retain their effects beyond the building, opening the possibility of a dungeon-delivery business and extending the Menagerie's reach beyond its street.

Arwin learns from the mesh that Earth has no magic and that he cannot return, so he accepts the Menagerie as his home while remaining determined to stop further child summons. The guild agrees that future sunset candidates must understand the danger and volunteer. Rodrick is selected next, but must arrange his intelligence network before leaving. Lillia launches magical food delivery into dungeons, supported by a communication and tracking system forged by Arwin and Wallace. Demand quickly exceeds expectations because delivery workers repeatedly rescue customers from dangerous encounters. At the same time, Ida warns that the Dwarven Council is watching the planned auction house. Rodrick proposes using a private auction and the promise of vault goods to turn the Council against House Blacktongue. He then leaves with Eleven for prolonged sunsetting preparation. Arwin, Wallace, and Koyu begin designing a powerful guardian body for the Devil's Den. In Esmerelda's shop, a cursed obsidian axe reacts first to Vanessa and then to Thane. Vanessa refuses the bloodthirsty devil within it, but the manifested entity realizes Thane triggered its awakening and claims him as its chosen wielder.

Thane refuses to submit to the weapon-devil and negotiates a binding contract that preserves control of his own body, though the exact terms remain private. The devil later consumes Lightfinger's magic and inhabits the sword, then begins teaching Thane to use his analytical gifts to influence outcomes. Thane insists on helping friends openly rather than manipulating them, prompting Lillia and Arwin to make time for shared forge work. Meanwhile, the prospective Devil's Den guardian receives a volatile core that must steep in Lillia's oven before its armor can be completed. Rodrick proves almost impossible for Two to prepare through conventional ordeals because he already possesses an extreme mental discipline developed through prior suffering. Two eventually accepts that he is ready. Arwin and Lillia jointly forge a concealed soul-armor core for Rodrick from night iron, his hair, and a color-shifting gemstone. As that work advances, Rodrick spends hours in the ley line and emerges standing despite intense pain. Two and Eleven take him onward to the final class-sunsetting stage, while his new armor awaits completion and his return.

Arwin and Lillia finish Rodrick's thin soul armor, which can hide beneath clothing, alter the wearer's shape, repair itself, and adapt to other protection. The Menagerie then divides responsibilities for the vault operation and the deception meant to draw House Blacktongue into conflict with the Dwarven Council. Before the mission begins, Arwin, Lillia, Wallace, Koyu, the Infernal Armory, and the Devil's Den core join in an exhausting shared forge. They complete a massive armored body, and its core awakens as the Devil's Den's manifested soul. The new guardian is not property: she is an autonomous transcendent being who agrees to defend the Den by choice and will kill only when she believes it necessary. The creation grants Arwin enough power to reshape himself. With no class restrictions guiding him, he increases his capacity and changes his blood into soul magma, reinforcing his body to contain the heat. Art then takes command of the planned deception. Ida has seeded the necessary information, the auction house is nearly built, and the true vault team has roughly two days to retrieve treasure and return before its absence becomes suspicious.

Arwin, Olive, Anna, and another Menagerie fighter follow a one-use key to a remote expert dungeon. After clearing its concealed undead, they open a hidden vault and confront an Expert Nine Golden Guardian powered by the treasure around it. Arwin's new body survives a devastating blow, and he summons Gehenna before crushing the guardian's head with Caldera. The group avoids a suspected greed trap by taking only portable magical objects and limited gold. At the same time, Art's decoy team carries fake treasure through a staged route. Blacktongue mercenaries attack, only to be killed by heavily armored dwarves from an apparent rogue Council faction. Rodrick, newly returned from successful sunsetting, uses his soul armor to impersonate Indrana and prevent the dwarves from seizing the decoy goods. An official Council delegation then reaches the Devil's Den. Lillia delays it until Arwin's real team returns and can prove the vault haul is genuine. The Menagerie secures formal Council backing and guards for the auction house in exchange for privileged access, with rare materials rather than gold serving as payment for VIP bids.

The Council-backed auction is delayed for two weeks while the Menagerie completes preparations. Rodrick reveals that sunsetting changed his class into an infiltrator and that his new armor can reproduce humanoid forms. Koyu is chosen for the next sunsetting slot because an ordinary crafted body would not solve the binding that limits his freedom. Carrying a stone from Menagerie Street, he successfully passes through Eleven's portal. Arwin turns next to awakening the auction house and binds its heart apparatus to Madiv. During the preparations, Thane identifies an unnatural group in the crowd and discovers an attempt to abduct any available Menagerie member. He permits his weapon-devil to take partial control, killing two attackers while preserving one. The survivor's relevant memories have been removed, leaving the sponsor unknown. Rodrick tightens security but uses the continuing preparations as bait. Arwin, Lillia, and Olive install the completed apparatus and name the venue the Mausoleum. Its violent awakening proves to be deliberate reshaping rather than collapse. The living building preserves all useful spaces, ejects its creators gently, and waits for Madiv, who accepts it as his own domain.

The awakened Mausoleum draws crowds and attention while Rodrick and Art watch for interference. Arwin prioritizes protection for Anna, whose role as the Menagerie's healer makes her an obvious target. Lillia completes another stage of her sunsetting and emerges with horns, heightened senses, faster reactions, and a living shadow, while her awareness of the Devil's Den expands across the growing street. Arwin, Wallace, and Vix use Anna's armor project to prepare Vix for the more dangerous work ahead. The completed soul-forged suit can protect and stabilize patients, store energy generated through healing, repair itself, and support Anna's emergency work. Vanessa, now employed by Esmerelda, continues sorting cursed weapons for the auction, while Madiv spends his time readying the Mausoleum. Vix defines the purpose of her replacement heart: she wants a deep energy reserve, sustained use of light and shadow, and freedom from constant magical rationing. After several failed designs, Arwin and Wallace settle on a core that gathers power from her body and surroundings. Vix accepts slower advancement as the price, and the surgical team prepares to begin.

During his sunsetting, Koyu rejects an offered body and chooses a stronger, fully awakened lich form, intending to have Arwin and Wallace craft his eventual body. He returns in time to protect Ida from a black-armored dwarf seeking the Mausoleum's weakness. Meanwhile, Anna sustains Vix as Arwin and Wallace remove her scarred heart and implant the soul-forged core. The bond nearly fails, but Koyu urges Vix to accept the core as part of herself. It ignites successfully, and Vix survives, though Anna forbids her from using magic during recovery. Rodrick and Olive defeat additional dwarven attackers, and Rodrick searches a captive's thoughts to identify the rival Council member behind the operation. The faction hoped to weaken Indrana by disrupting the Menagerie's auction. Rodrick ends the immediate threat by showing the rival that he knows of the man's hidden son and can locate him, without directly threatening the child. The Menagerie closes the numbered story preparing layered auction security, including a staged deterrent for thieves. Its members remain alive, the Council rival is expected to stand down, and the auction is still approaching.

characters.description: A ruler believed dead after escaping King Caydean. Injured and low on power, he seeks dwarven knowledge that might counter Daemons while sustaining the infant dragon magically bound to him. His survival remains hidden from his wider circle of allies.
characters.name: Rezkin

characters.description: An elven general and path builder who helped Rezkin escape King Caydean. She hides Rezkin's survival, seeks aid from her own people, and joins him in searching for a weapon against the Daemon threat. She and Rezkin have also become romantic partners.
characters.name: Azeria

characters.description: A young dragon linked to Rezkin and able to speak into his mind. She depends on power drawn through their bond, creating a dangerous drain that Rezkin cannot end by simply leaving her behind. Despite the risk, he is committed to keeping her with him.
characters.name: Sina

characters.description: The ruler of Asshai and the immediate enemy pursuing Rezkin. His combined Spiritua and Daemon power overwhelms Rezkin, and his larger purpose remains concealed. His forces believe Rezkin dead after their confrontation.
characters.name: King Caydean

characters.description: A veteran warrior, archer, and wind mage who swears to protect Azeria's secrets and joins her expedition to Grestag.
characters.name: Azeria's former mentor

characters.description: A high king consulted by Azeria about the Daemon threat. He recalls that the earlier war turned only after the Daemon king fell and directs her toward the nearly lost craft of the dwarves, whose weapons and machines may still hold useful answers.
characters.name: The elven ruler

characters.description: An ally investigating King Caydean's plans with Malcius. She reports that his faction manipulated a royal succession to secure a large shipment of purple metal that absorbs magical power. Rezkin gives the investigators a relay for urgent contact.
characters.name: Yserria

characters.description: Yserria's partner in tracing King Caydean's acquisition of power-absorbing metal. He helps establish that Caydean's faction manipulated succession trials to obtain it, and receives a modified relay for urgent contact with Rezkin.
characters.name: Malcius

characters.description: A surviving engineer who maintains the defensive machines of Grestag. Bitter over his people's near extinction and distrustful of elves, he initially refuses help but agrees to demonstrate dwarven equipment made to resist Daemons.
characters.name: The dwarf engineer

characters.description: The surviving dwarf engineer in Grestag. He explains that dwarven metal stores magical energy, powers the city's machines, and resists Daemon power. He offers armor and up to one hundred machines for the war, provided Rezkin's group can secure a sufficiently large energy source.
characters.name: Haggish

characters.description: A young dwarf trained in smithing and combat who is sent beyond Grestag to build alliances for her dwindling people. Her crystal-tipped staff can connect armor and machines to an external magical source.
characters.name: The dwarven apprentice

characters.description: A resistance battle mage trying to release people from coerced oaths to King Caydean. His first experimental attempt kills the captive, deepening his fear of both his destructive power and the choices the war demands.
characters.name: Wesson

characters.description: A returning ally who works beside Wesson in the resistance. He accepts the hazards of sending a potentially compromised mage back into King Caydean's service and urges Wesson to use the opportunity for intelligence.
characters.name: Farson

characters.description: A battle mage whose oath may still compel loyalty to King Caydean. She asks to return as a possible spy, and Wesson agrees to prepare a secured relay despite the risk that her oath could compromise her reports. Her loyalties therefore remain uncertain.
characters.name: The returning battle mage

characters.description: Rezkin's missing ally, discovered alive in compelled Fae service. His unusual ability to understand the Fae and move through their overlapping world has made him their human liaison and a general in training.
characters.name: Tam

characters.description: A Crimson Blades thief assigned to obtain supplies and assist Wesson's covert research into magical oaths. He knows Wesson only as a mage working on the Raven's behalf and does not know that Rezkin never authorized the experiments.
characters.name: Remy

characters.description: A powerful healer permitted to train as a battle mage under King Caydean's revised rules. He is assigned to partner the battle mage who has returned to Kaibain, then leads her away from the palace to see what he presents as a historic site.
characters.name: Silas

characters.description: A rare siphon Daemon forced into the returning battle mage. It can preserve abilities gained through former hosts, including the craft needed to forge King Caydean's enchanted metal. Its new host remains aware but cannot always control her own body.
characters.name: The Smith

characters.description: A wary magical teacher who accepts Rezkin as an apprentice while watching for signs that his increasing power is driving him toward madness. The instructor supplies him with the order's trackable gear and continues testing his control.
characters.name: Rezkin's Spiritua instructor

characters.description: An allied mage working undercover near King Caydean's palace. She tracks confirmed cases of possession, including temple priests, but argues that a human host should not be condemned solely because a Daemon occupies the body.
characters.name: Wesson's undercover contact

characters.description: A relay worker coerced into an oath to King Caydean and targeted by Wesson's experimental release spell. She appears to die when it fails, then escapes with knowledge of Wesson's identity and wanted status.
characters.name: The escaped relay worker

characters.description: Rezkin's cousin and the effective regent of Kyle during his apparent death. Rezkin keeps him in that office after returning, valuing his governance while recognizing his limited experience in war. He reports the scale and strategy of the Asshai blockade.
characters.name: Tieran Nirius

characters.description: An escaped captive and royal claimant who is formally introduced as Rezkin's older brother. Rather than accept hostile accounts of Rezkin, he asks to judge his younger brother for himself after reaching safety in Kyle.
characters.name: Prince Thresson

characters.description: A Daemon-possessed general overseeing the immense spell nexus built into Kaibain's temple. She recognizes Wesson's apparent Daemon identity and confines him in the chamber that powers the construct, where his attempts to cast are absorbed.
characters.name: Caydean's temple general

characters.description: One of the twin allies on Rezkin's temple escape team. Released Daemon power possesses him during the retreat, and he immediately turns against Rezkin. He remains alive, and Rezkin treats finding a way to save him as a priority.
characters.name: The possessed twin

description.text: The seventh entry in the series picks up as Rezkin and the Ielvanen general Azeria recover from a failed confrontation with King Caydean, whose combined Spiritua and Daemon power has proven too strong to face directly. With his bonded dragon Sina increasingly dependent on his magic for survival, Rezkin needs a decisive advantage against Caydean and the wider Daemon threat. Guided toward the isolated ruins of Grestag, he and his companions seek out the nearly extinct dwarves, whose surviving craft may hold weapons effective against demons, gaining new allies including a wary dwarven engineer and a young apprentice willing to join the cause. A separate thread follows Wesson's dangerous attempts to break the magical oaths binding enemy mages into forced service, while Rezkin secures a bargain with the Fae for a vital source of magical power at the cost of a future obligation.

recaps.ending: Kyle is no longer under blockade, and Tieran Nirius remains regent while Rezkin leads the larger war. Azeria is Rezkin's empress and life-bonded partner. Tam has learned that he is partly Fae and can command the elemental forces placed under him, though he still must master that authority. Dwarven machines have a prospective power source, individual elven allies have joined Rezkin, and the Spiritua support his command, but the elven nation has not entered the war. In Kaibain, the temple ritual succeeds despite the infiltration. Daemon power spreads through the crowded city, one of Rezkin's twin allies becomes possessed, and a mass method of removing Daemons from their hosts is urgently needed. Rezkin escapes with his bonded dragon and a rune-marked ritual key after badly wounding King Caydean, whose missing body leaves his fate uncertain. Wesson does not reach the escape portal and remains somewhere inside Kaibain. Finding him, understanding the key, and containing the possession crisis are the immediate unresolved tasks.
recaps.in_short: Rezkin survives King Caydean's attack and assembles dwarven, Fae, elven, and Spiritua support for the Daemon war. He and Azeria enter a life bond, return to Kyle as emperor and empress, and break the Asshai blockade with help from Tam's newly awakened Fae authority. Meanwhile, Wesson's attempts to free oath-bound mages expose his own Daemon bond and produce oath transfer rather than freedom. Caydean, himself inhabited by a Daemon ruler, turns Kaibain's new temple into a vast nexus. Rezkin's team attacks during its opening ritual, but the nexus releases Daemon power across the city. Rezkin wounds Caydean and escapes with the ritual key and his bonded dragon, yet Caydean's survival is unknown, one ally is possessed, and Wesson is left behind in Kaibain.

recaps.text: Previously: Rezkin became ruler of Kyle while opposing King Caydean, whose campaign threatened Rezkin's allies and the wider realm. Rezkin's apparent death left his cousin Tieran Nirius governing Kyle as regent. Farson and Wesson continued resistance work, while Yserria and Malcius remained allied investigators, all without knowing Rezkin had survived. Prince Thresson, another royal claimant, remained caught in the consequences of Caydean's rule. Tam was missing from Rezkin's wider circle. Rezkin had also formed a magical bond with an infant dragon, creating a new responsibility that could not easily be set aside. His allies were scattered across political, magical, and military fronts, with Kyle forced to endure the effects of losing its ruler. Their obligations remained unresolved. The struggle now extends beyond rival thrones: Daemon influence has become a direct danger, and the alliances, magical knowledge, and military power needed to confront it are still divided.

Rezkin escapes King Caydean badly injured, accompanied by Azeria and his bonded infant dragon. Caydean's Spiritua and Daemon strength is greater than theirs, while the dragon's need for magical energy is steadily weakening Rezkin. Azeria conceals his survival and learns that dwarven craft may offer the best surviving defense against Daemons. She, her former mentor, Rezkin, and the dragon travel to Grestag. Yserria and Malcius separately uncover Caydean's acquisition of a large shipment of purple metal that absorbs power, though its intended use remains unknown. Grestag's defensive machines nearly kill the travelers before Rezkin reaches a surviving dwarf engineer. The dwarves explain that their metal stores magical energy and resists Daemon attacks. They make fitted armor for the party and offer as many as one hundred machines, but operating them requires an immense source of power. A dangerous spring between realms may supply it. A young dwarven apprentice joins Rezkin with a staff designed to connect such a source to dwarven armor and machinery.

Wesson begins trying to free battle mages from oaths to King Caydean. His first attempt kills the captive, but he continues the research and equips a potentially compromised battle mage to return as a spy. Farson accepts the danger as necessary intelligence work. Rezkin's party enters the Fae forest seeking the spring needed to power the dwarven machines. There Rezkin discovers Tam alive. Tam can understand the Fae and has been pressed into serving as their liaison and military trainee. Rezkin secures access to the spring by agreeing that Tam will command a future force shared by humans and Fae. Azeria objects to the bargain but remains committed to acting beside Rezkin. She and Rezkin also acknowledge their romantic attachment, though they postpone a life bond because either partner would die soon after the other. Rezkin then takes Tam to Kaibain for practical training. With magical aid from Rezkin and Wesson, Tam kills a Daemon's human host and drives the entity back to its own realm. The encounter proves that ordinary troops cannot face even a weak Daemon without magical protection, sharpening Rezkin's need for a broader supernatural alliance.

Wesson continues lethal oath-breaking trials in secret while Kaibain fills with hungry pilgrims and immigrants drawn by King Caydean's mandates. His battle-mage spy passes a truth-tested debriefing and is assigned to Silas, a healer trained for combat. Silas reveals himself as a servant of the Daemon ruler inhabiting Caydean. He and his accomplices force a siphon Daemon called the Smith into the spy. The host remains aware but cannot always control her body. Because the Smith retains skills from earlier hosts, it can forge the enchanted metal required for Caydean's concealed project. It preserves Wesson's relay as a useful path to the rebels. Elsewhere, Rezkin's party reaches the inter-realm spring but finds it guarded by a powerful being and altered creatures. The dwarven apprentice succeeds in linking her staff to the spring, securing the prospective energy source. During the fight Rezkin enters the spring to save his dragon companion and releases its power against the guardian. Both survive, but any lasting effects of the exposure remain unknown. Azeria takes them to her people's capital for treatment, exposing Rezkin's survival there. A wary elven leader then agrees to train Rezkin in exchange for political independence and Rezkin's submission to magical and combat instruction.

Training pushes Rezkin toward exhaustion and emotions he has long suppressed. He and Azeria choose a mutual life bond that joins their reserves and makes each dependent on the other's survival. Rezkin becomes a Spiritua apprentice while hiding the full speed of his progress. In restricted records he discovers evidence of an old attempt to remove a Daemon from a living host. The elven ruler admits that the procedure expelled the Daemon but destroyed the woman's independent will, and his people now execute possessed hosts instead. Rezkin insists that the failed method should be improved rather than abandoned. The ruler will not commit the whole nation to war, though individuals may join Rezkin. In Kaibain, Wesson learns that possession is widespread around the palace and temple. His attempt to free a coerced relay worker appears to kill her, but she revives or survives and escapes after identifying him as wanted. Rezkin's dragon companion recovers from the spring much larger and able to speak, though still young in mind. Rezkin finally reveals his true skill to his instructor in a duel. After hearing Rezkin's purpose, the instructor places Spiritua support under his command. Rezkin prepares to return to Kyle with Azeria and the dragon.

Rezkin returns to Kyle during an Asshai blockade and formally meets Prince Thresson as his older brother. He resumes the throne, names Azeria empress, and keeps Tieran Nirius as regent while he conducts the war. In Kaibain, Rezkin reveals his survival to Farson and Wesson. Farson renews his allegiance, and a Spiritua identifies Wesson as a complete human bound to a powerful Daemon nature. Investigation of Caydean's temple becomes urgent. Wesson's undercover contact is temporarily controlled by a Daemon opposed to Caydean's Daemon ruler. It warns that the temple opening will activate a major nexus built with enchanted metal. Wesson also recaptures the relay worker from his experiment and discovers that he transferred her oath from Caydean to himself instead of breaking it. She reluctantly returns to enemy service as his agent. Rezkin then attacks the blockade with a new mage-crewed warship, portal teams, Spiritua, and Fae support under Tam. Tam's elemental forces grow into a storm that threatens both fleets, but he discovers that he is partly Fae and commands them to stop. The blockade is shattered, prisoners are secured, survivors are rescued, and Kyle's sea access is restored.

Rezkin leads teams into Kaibain to disrupt the temple opening. Wesson enters openly by impersonating the Daemon lord that the possessed congregation believes him to be. The temple's Daemon-held general confirms that the entire building is a spell nexus made from enchanted-metal runes, then traps Wesson in a siphon chamber where every spell he casts feeds the ritual. Rezkin's tunnel team reaches the central chamber, and Azeria and other allies infiltrate among the ritual priests. When the ceremony begins, Wesson devises a tiny lightning construct that releases a captive Daemon and creates a distraction. Rezkin attacks King Caydean on the nexus platform, but the ritual begins draining Wesson's Daemon power and completes despite the fighting. A wave of Daemon power spreads over Kaibain. Rezkin overloads his black blade, breaks Caydean's weapon, and knocks him from the temple. Caydean's body disappears before his death can be confirmed. Rezkin takes the ritual key and orders a retreat. During the escape, released power possesses one of the twin allies and turns him hostile. Rezkin escapes with his bonded dragon, but Wesson never reaches the portal and is left behind. With much of crowded Kaibain potentially possessed, Rezkin now needs a scalable exorcism, a way to save his ally, and a means to recover Wesson and understand the key.

characters.description: An Army combat medic serving with a helicopter response crew. He treats soldiers wounded by an explosive attack and helps evacuate the most critical casualties before a rocket strikes the aircraft.
characters.name: Sergeant Nelson

characters.description: The medic previously introduced as Sergeant Nelson. Left quadriplegic after the helicopter crash, Joe accepts an irreversible transfer into Eternium so he can regain a working body and continue living in the immersive world.
characters.name: Joe

characters.description: A former medic colleague of Joe who now works for the company behind Eternium. The colleague offers Joe permanent entry into the immersive world.
characters.name: Former Medic Colleague

characters.description: Joe's primary caregiver during the months after his disabling injury.
characters.name: Joe's Mother

characters.description: Joe's wife, who seeks an annulment and leaves shortly after he wakes following the helicopter crash.
characters.name: Joe's Wife

characters.description: A weakened deity associated with concealed knowledge, water, and darkness. The god offers Joe the hidden Ritualist class in exchange for his allegiance and requires him to keep both the class and their relationship secret.
characters.name: Hidden God

characters.description: A powerful Wanderers member who recognizes the value of Joe's healing, recruits him, and becomes the leader of his field party.
characters.name: Tiona

characters.description: The officer responsible for Ardania's guard training. Joe earns his trust by healing far more guards than required, and the captain rewards him with useful clerical equipment.
characters.name: Guard Captain

characters.description: Tiona's heavily armored frontline fighter. Joe risks leaving formation to save him during an early hunt, establishing mutual trust between the two teammates.
characters.name: Dylan

characters.description: The ranger and archer in Tiona's field party. He scouts targets and fights from range during the group's hunts, forming part of the team that helps Joe adjust to combat and advancement in Eternium.
characters.name: Chad

characters.description: Leader of the player-killing Hardcores guild. After killing Joe's teammates, he tries to force Joe into his guild and threatens further abuse when Joe refuses, making the conflict between them direct and personal.
characters.name: Headshot

characters.description: Ardania's head librarian and a guide to Joe's scholarly development. He grants Joe access to the library and assigns work intended to prepare him for a future profession centered on study and recovered knowledge.
characters.name: Boris

characters.description: An alchemist who sells Joe monster cores and permits him to use a restricted ritual component inside the shop. Joe's unusually demanding ritual draws his professional interest in the novice's future progress.
characters.name: Jake

characters.description: The merchant who runs Odds and Ends. The owner wagers a spatial ring that Joe cannot create a ritual capable of organizing the shop.
characters.name: Odds and Ends Owner

characters.description: A Wanderers officer who brings Joe into the displaced guild on favorable terms.
characters.name: Aten

characters.description: The quiet rogue in Tiona's party. Guess uses a male avatar and communicates through typed messages rendered in a mechanical voice, while contributing stealth and precise attacks to the team's wolfman hunts.
characters.name: Guess

characters.description: The name revealed for Joe's secret deity, previously known only as the Hidden God. Tatum advises Joe to cultivate his unique abilities and gives him a sigil that converts a share of earned experience into divine favor.
characters.name: Tatum

characters.description: A licensed Wanderers mage and officer-in-training. She teaches Joe to locate, condense, and manipulate his mana while working off the debt created when Aten and the guild financed her Mage's College education.
characters.name: Terra

characters.description: A skilled armor smith who repairs captured wolfman equipment. After learning that Dylan is pursuing a defensive role, the smith offers a specialized route that could provide the protection needed for pain-realistic frontline combat.
characters.name: Smith

characters.description: The ruler of Ardania, who receives the newly noble Wanderers for a confidential briefing. She explains the existential conflict between the human and wolfman nations and offers the guild a secret royal mission.
characters.name: Queen of Ardania

characters.description: A wind-and-fire mage captured after entering Joe's protected workshop and trying to attack him. Cel claims the Mage's College is pursuing Joe for forbidden ritual practice and remains hostile while Joe confines and questions him.
characters.name: Cel

characters.description: Cel's senior instructor at the Mage's College. Believing his apprentice dead, he attacks Joe, then agrees to escort Joe to the college after learning Cel is alive. His conduct is constrained by the institution's magical Accords.
characters.name: Master of Fire

characters.description: The head of the Mage's College tribunal. He oversees coercive proceedings against Cel and Joe, imposes a severe sentence on Joe, and prepares to bind him publicly through the college's Accords.
characters.name: Archmage

description.text: After an IED and helicopter strike leave Army medic Joe Nelson paralyzed and his marriage ended, he accepts an irreversible offer to transfer his mind permanently into the immersive game Eternium, a one-way trade that destroys his real body in exchange for a mobile new life. Rather than take a standard class, Joe completes every optional starting trial, becoming the first of over a million players to do so, and is then approached by a mysterious Hidden God offering the secret Ritualist class in exchange for uncovering forbidden knowledge. Presenting himself publicly only as a cleric to avoid prejudice against his true class, Joe joins the Wanderers guild, earns his place through healing in early monster fights, and begins drawing the attention of both grateful allies and a hostile player-killing guild determined to force him into its ranks.

recaps.ending: Joe uses his single contractual escape to destroy the Accords without suffering their contract-based consequences. The compelled mages are freed, and the Archmage admits that he enslaved the Mage's College and withheld its power from Ardania's war. When he tries to destroy the city, the stored mana system overloads and kills him. The college agrees to broaden access, reduce costs, share research, and aid the kingdom. Cel is free after his coerced promotion, while the Master of Fire removes Joe's temporary Warlock title. Joe and the Wanderers receive public credit and exceptional standing. Tatum makes Joe his Chosen, advances his public class to Arc Cleric, and grants him daily Resurrection, while Joe's true Ritualist and Occultist paths remain concealed. Aten's guild continues the secret Shatter a People campaign against the Wolfman Nation. Tiona has left the old party for Royal Guard-linked training, Dylan has renewed confidence as a Bulwark, and the later paths of Dylan, Chad, and Guess are not settled. Terra still owes service for her college training. Joe ends at level nine, seeking magical instruction and a dependable ritual team that can eventually become a powerful coven. His possible return to reality, Tatum's restoration, the Hardcores conflict, Seeker of Truth, and the war all remain open.
recaps.in_short: Army medic Joe is paralyzed after a helicopter attack and permanently transfers into Eternium, where he becomes a concealed Ritualist serving the forgotten deity Tatum while publicly appearing to be a cleric and scholar. He joins the Wanderers, develops healing and ritual abilities, survives player killers, helps make night travel possible, and supports Tiona's party through a growing conflict with wolfmen. Joe captures an enemy altar for Tatum and redirects its summoned creatures against the Wolfman Nation, shortly before the Wanderers accept the royal quest Shatter a People and his party separates. Working alone, he captures the mage Cel and uncovers the Accords that magically control the Mage's College. Joe destroys the Accords using a one-use escape from contractual penalties, freeing the mages. The Archmage dies during a failed attempt to destroy Ardania, and the college begins reform. Joe and the Wanderers receive public credit.
