description.text: The fourth entry in the series opens with Earth at peace after the war of earlier books, and Jack Rust newly a father to twins with his partner Vivi. Restless to keep growing and fulfill an old obligation, Jack leaves his family to travel with Brock and a mysterious mentor called the Sage to the Black Hole Church, an isolated faction hidden inside a black hole where gravity and cultivation pressure are extreme. Registered as an outer disciple with an unusual starting rank that makes him a target for hostile rivals, Jack accepts a lethal duel with a bullying senior disciple while working to protect a vulnerable friend and searching for resources to fund his next breakthrough. Exploring an unconventional use of his rare healing artifact alongside punishing physical conditioning, Jack prepares to face his rival in a confrontation whose outcome will shape his standing within the Church.

recaps.ending: Jack passes Archon Green Dragon's trial by asserting a personal, fist-centered Dao, then refines and absorbs the realm heart. The inheritance raises him to five fruits, gives him control over the realm's exits, and leaves him with B-grade fighting power. He releases Brock and Min Ling, and the three head first toward Earth before planning further travel. Min Ling accepts that Jack is married and does not pursue her feelings. Jack deliberately leaves Spacewind and the rest of the expedition in Green Cultivator Town until he can safely deal with Spacewind, though he intends eventually to free those who did not attack his group. The Archon's realm can survive for millennia, and Jack is expected to return at A-grade to incorporate it into his inner world. The life-drop guardian remains asleep, Jack still owes the Supreme Blood a lethal repayment debt, and his promises to Dorman Whistles remain outstanding. Elsewhere, the Second Crusade seizes the Black Hole Church Cathedral after its guardian dies covering an evacuation. Boatman, the Sage, and other Church survivors are unaccounted for. A disgraced former Animal Kingdom warden orders a search for Earth, placing Vivi, Abel, Eric, and the relocated world in renewed danger.
recaps.in_short: After securing relocated Earth, Jack Rust leaves Vivi and their newborn twins to train at the Black Hole Church with Brock. He survives a hostile Cathedral culture, reaches C-grade, creates a trade in healing stones, wins a world anchor, and becomes Boatman's disciple. A joint expedition with the Hand of God enters a hidden realm that proves to be an Archon's creation. Baron Longform dies after ambushing Jack and Brock, while Min Ling saves them and joins their party. Trapped in the realm's deepest trial, Jack defines his personal fist-centered Dao, claims the realm heart, becomes the Archon's heir, and emerges with five fruits and B-grade combat power. He, Brock, and Min Ling leave for Earth, but Spacewind and most of the expedition remain confined. Meanwhile, the Second Crusade captures the Church's Cathedral, and a former Animal Kingdom warden begins searching for Earth to strike Jack's family.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Rust helped move Earth beyond System space and defended it from the Animal Kingdom, leaving the planet temporarily secure but isolated from the wider order. He carries an extraordinary life artifact, has ties to the Black Hole Church, and remains an outlaw in the System's view. Brock is his brorilla companion and closest cultivation ally, with a growing community of bros around him. Vivi is Jack's partner, while Margaret Rust, Edgar, Harambe, Gan Salin, and other allies help form Earth's new foundation. Former enemies have been defeated, captured, or driven away, yet the Animal Kingdom remains hostile and the planet's safety still depends heavily on Jack's strength. He has reached peak D-grade and must stabilize his cultivation before advancing. The Black Hole Church offers a route toward greater power, but following it will take him away from the people he has fought to protect.

Vivi gives birth to Jack's twins during Earth's first peaceful months after relocation. Jack nevertheless leaves with Brock and the Sage, travelling through many interspace layers to the Black Hole Church Cathedral inside a black hole. The Cathedral's crushing gravity and competitive hierarchy immediately expose how small their strength is on a universal scale. Jack becomes an outer disciple and is placed at rank 950 by the Head Envoy, gaining limited access to the Heavy Pagoda while provoking disciples who consider the placement undeserved. He defeats a C-grade will cultivator whose Truth Domain tries to exploit uncertainty in his convictions. The victory earns a Dao Stone but draws attention from her powerful husband. Dorman Whistles then arrives, heavily altered by a trapped treasure and unable to pursue his former speed-based path. Jack learns that low-ranked disciples cannot use the Cathedral teleporters, so returning to Vivi and the children now depends on both reaching C-grade and climbing above rank 800. The Heavy Pagoda may reduce the resources required for his breakthrough, and Jack promises to help Dorman if he succeeds.

Don Cranxiao, a three-fruit enforcer hired against Jack, repeatedly attacks Dorman and uses him as leverage. Jack accepts a lethal duel carrying a twenty-Dao-stone debt, then brings Dorman into his cabin with Brock. Attempts to develop conventional healing prove too slow, but Jack learns to compress life energy into healing stones. The guardian inside his artifact identifies it as the Supreme Blood, restricts his production, and hints at a stronger use. Jack discovers that he can fuse life energy permanently into his body, increasing his physical attributes outside ordinary System advancement. Two weeks of punishing tempering let him withstand the Cathedral's gravity without Dao and survive a higher Heavy Pagoda floor. When Cranxiao returns, Baron Longform appears as his cousin and protector. Jack chooses to fight immediately, overpowers Cranxiao's tyrannical domain and weapon with his enhanced body and four-armed form, and kills him under the duel terms. Longform pays the wager but openly declares Jack an enemy, while many low-ranked disciples begin treating Jack as their champion.

Jack's new body and life artifact carry him to rank 675 in the Ceaseless Murder Globe, unlocking unrestricted Cathedral teleporters and better training facilities. Rather than return home immediately, he spends twenty-two Dao Stones on his C-grade breakthrough. The process nearly tears apart his soul world and subjects him to a foundational trial of the Fist. After two external months of failure, he realizes he is not meant to reproduce an absolute ideal. He must affirm his own distinct fist path. That conviction forms his first Dao fruit and advances him to C-grade. Jack chooses the Gladiator Titan, King class and reunites with Brock and Dorman. Marcus William, a six-fruit swordsman and husband of Jack's earlier opponent, challenges him over their dispute. Jack refuses a delay, defeats Marcus despite the five-fruit gap, and wins a fifty-stone wager that Marcus partly pays through future wages. Brock remains at the Cathedral to earn status independently, while Jack finally teleports back to Earth. Elsewhere, three explorers discover a portal to an unknown hidden realm and plan to report it to competing major factions.

Jack reunites with Vivi, his infant children, and Margaret Rust, supplying Earth with healing and cultivation resources before returning to the Cathedral. During his absence, Brock manifests the Bro Code in the Ceaseless Murder Globe and earns recognition as an outer disciple. Jack uses the Fallen Genius Mirror, where visions of failed cultivators force him to acknowledge how often chance has shaped survival. He decides that danger does not change his chosen path. Further Globe victories raise him to rank 216 and stabilize his first Dao fruit. The Head Envoy then announces a joint Black Hole Church and Hand of God expedition to an upper-B-grade hidden realm, led by Spacewind, with Min Ling commanding the Church's C-grades if they separate. Jack is publicly offered a rare world anchor, valuable both to his current foundation and an eventual B-grade breakthrough, but only if he reaches the top 100 within a year. The announcement makes him a target for nearly every ambitious disciple. He rejects the chance to withdraw and accepts the deadline, while temporary rules forbid direct assaults during the competition.

Most of Jack's followers leave when the world-anchor contest puts them under pressure, but Brock, Dorman, and several others remain. Baron Longform finances a seven-fruit challenger and blocks Jack's preferred Dao Chamber bookings. Jack studies mortal lives to create Fist of Mortality, then makes a dangerous bargain with the Supreme Blood's guardian: he may produce one healing stone per day, but must repay twice the borrowed energy within two years or die. The Sage fronts the trade while Brock organizes distribution, providing enough Dao Stones to fund Jack's training and Brock's C-grade advance. Jack deepens his space comprehension, strengthens his body, and forms Space as his second fruit. At the scheduled duel, he expands the contest into a Cathedral-wide sequence carrying the world anchor as its stake. He defeats the original swordswoman, twenty-five registered challengers, and an additional veteran swordsman despite mounting exhaustion. The Head Envoy awards him the world anchor and six months of free Dao Chamber use. Jack absorbs it into his soul world, refining his Dao, improving his affinity with life, and preparing the foundation for an eventual inner world.

During the final six months before departure, Jack reaches rank 98, accumulates extensive resources, and forms a third fruit of life. He and Brock visit Earth, where Jack spends two weeks with Vivi, Abel, Eric, and his other allies before leaving without knowing when he can return. Thirty Church C-grades gather for the hidden-realm expedition under Spacewind, whose hostility toward Jack comes from jealousy over Min Ling. Boatman provides the starship. At the destination, the Church meets a Hand of God force and holds exhibition spars under a fragile agreement to cooperate. A venomous Hand prodigy deliberately maims Church opponents until Boatman orders Jack to intervene. Jack overwhelms her, prompting her A-grade master to attempt retaliation. Boatman blocks the attack and asks Jack to become his direct disciple, preventing a wider clash. In private, he makes clear that the choice is voluntary and that he will teach rather than rescue Jack from self-created danger. Jack accepts. Boatman gives him an inheritance seed and a cube of concentrated death energy to support a life-and-death foundation beneath his Fist Dao. The expedition then passes through the portal into the hidden realm.

The expedition arrives in a vast living jungle that appears to be an A-grade cultivator's inner world, with no portal remaining behind them. The B-grades head toward the core while C-grade teams spread out. Jack and Brock spare a tree dragon and share its ripe Dao fruits, then Jack begins learning the death technique Nihility from Boatman's cube. At a volcano, Brock discovers that the apparent treasure is a crystal-producing tree enslaved by a B-grade red dragon. He forms a voluntary alliance with its twig-like offspring. During the joint assault, Jack and Brock take six fruits while leaving the tree enough to survive, but Baron Longform traps them below the lava. Longform rejects compromise and attacks for revenge. The allied twigs intervene, yet Longform sacrifices lifespan and a Dao fruit for greater power, gravely injuring Brock. Jack creates Supernova from space, death, and stellar insight, leaving both himself and Longform incapacitated. When the others arrive, the Hand of God leader uses the missing treasure as a pretext to attack Church members. Min Ling breaks Jack and Brock out of a spatial cage and flees with them into deeper lava. Before escaping, Jack kills the critically weakened Longform.

Min Ling carries Jack and Brock through more than a hundred miles of lava and into the hidden realm's core temple. Jack recovers, shares the stolen fruits equally, and advances to four fruits, adding death to fist, space, and life. Min Ling reaches eight fruits, but the temple's guardians are dangerous even to B-grades. The trio catches up with the surviving B-grade expedition and is allowed into its formation on the condition that they neither fight nor retain discoveries. Spacewind and the Hand of God leader use weaker members as trap scouts and confiscate finds. A late B-grade black dragon then seals the group in battle. Spacewind forces several Church members to detonate their inner worlds against it. Jack protects Brock and Min Ling from the final shockwave with Supernova and regenerates only because the Supreme Blood's guardian intervenes, exhausting itself into slumber. After the dragon dies, the leaders imprison everyone until three patterned cubes can be solved. Jack recognizes their relationship to Boatman's Death Cube. After three months, he completes their life patterns, arranges a diversion, and opens the remaining cubes for his party. Jack, Brock, and Min Ling escape with a green bean and a wooden key while all nine surviving B-grades pursue them.

Spacewind and the Hand of God leader recover the first cube's treasure and identify Jack's party as the thieves. With ordinary exits blocked, Jack, Brock, and Min Ling flee through a forbidden shaft radiating A-grade pressure. They survive Spacewind's final attack and land in a sealed lava cavern dominated by an immense tree. A dead prisoner left evidence that a wooden key from above could activate it. Jack uses the key, and a message from Archon Green Dragon identifies the hidden realm as an inheritance site. Escape now requires Jack to decipher space-time runes and qualify to refine the Dragon Life Realm Heart. The activation severs the entire realm from the outside universe, trapping the other expedition members as well and defeating every attempted rescue. Over three years, Jack matures his fourth fruit, Brock reaches the same cultivation boundary, and Min Ling develops a ninth fruit. Jack finally resolves the spatial locks without force and enters the tree through a hidden corridor. At the realm's core, he chooses the inheritance attempt instead of an available departure. The numbered story ends with Jack transported alone before projections of the twelve old gods, while Brock and Min Ling wait outside and the sealed realm remains beyond outside help.

description.text: The fifth entry in the series finds Jack Rust returning to civilization after years away, only to learn that the Hand of God has crushed the Black Hole Church and is hunting its scattered allies across the galaxy. Traveling in disguise with Brock and old companions, Jack fights his way past hostile patrols to reach the ruins of a former ally faction, searching for the missing mentor who alone knows the hidden coordinates that lead back to Earth. As his identity becomes known and powerful pursuers close in, Jack is forced deeper into hostile territory, testing untested space-time abilities and risking increasingly dangerous confrontations in his effort to protect his family and find a way home.

recaps.ending: Jack ends the Animal Kingdom war by destroying its elder corps, killing Eva Solvig and the surviving founders, and leaving Artis Emberheart permanently sealed in intergalactic emptiness. Brock, Gan Salin, Nauja, and their companions stop Jack from extending his vengeance to civilians. The surviving Emberheart family abandons its name and becomes Open Chest. Jack returns to Earth, reunites with Vivi and Abel, buries an empty casket for Eric, and says goodbye before departing with Brock and Dorman Whistles. Min Ling, the Sage, and Sovereign Heavenly Spoon carry them toward the Black Hole Church's hidden forces. Brock becomes B-grade with an 8,800-mile inner world. Jack's freedom-based tenth fruit helps him advance to B-grade and expand his inner world to 10,000 miles, after which he survives heavenly tribulation with Brock and Boatman's intervention. Earth remains vulnerable, Black Hole World's people still await rescue, and Copy Jack and the sentient stone remain unexplained. The Heaven Immortal prepares mass slaughter while an anti-immortal queen mobilizes an opposing army and eleven old gods move toward system space.
recaps.in_short: Jack Rust emerges from a hidden realm and fights through the Hand of God's conquered territory to reach Earth. Artis Emberheart kidnaps and kills Jack's son Eric, cracking Jack's Dao and driving him into the Animal Abyss, which leads to the sealed Black Hole World. Jack repairs himself, promises to free its stranded people, and returns to wage war on the Animal Kingdom. He defeats its ancestors and Eva Solvig, while Brock stops him from killing Emberheart civilians. Artis is sealed and abandoned alive, and the survivors renounce their family name. After mourning Eric with Vivi and Abel, Jack leaves Earth for the Second Crusade. Brock reaches B-grade with an 8,800-mile inner world. Jack discovers freedom as a tenth Dao fruit, forms a 10,000-mile inner world, and survives heavenly tribulation with Brock and Boatman's help. As the Church prepares for war, immortal and anti-immortal armies mobilize and eleven old gods approach system space.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Rust, also known as Lionel Horseman, became an Earth cultivator and a disciple of the Black Hole Church. Brock became his spiritually linked brorilla brother, while Min Ling, Gan Salin, and Nauja were among his trusted allies. Jack's enemies included Artis Emberheart and the wider Emberheart line. Jack left Earth and spent years away in a hidden realm, while his partner Vivi raised their children, Abel and Eric. The route home remained difficult, and the safety of Jack's family continued to guide his choices.

Jack, Brock, and Min Ling leave the hidden realm in disguise and reach Vengalo, where Gan Salin and Nauja recognize them. The reunited travellers learn that the Hand of God has captured the Black Hole Church Cathedral, scattered the Exploding Sun, and begun a purge directed in the Milky Way by Artis Emberheart. Min Ling departs to check on her people, while Nauja helps the others seize a Falling Star teleporter. Jack and Brock defeat the defenders, and the group escapes into the Milky Way, exposing Jack's return. Earth remains hidden and mobile, and Jack cannot contact it without one of the few people who knows its frequency. The group searches the ruined Exploding Sun headquarters for Jack's missing former master. Brock, Gan Salin, and Nauja destroy the Hand of God outpost occupying the site, but Jack finds only a cryptic clue. Artis and a late B-grade Hand commander arrive too late to catch them, leaving the group without a confirmed route home and under a widening hunt.

The clue sends Jack's group toward a meteor near Hell. On the way, Jack studies the Animal Abyss and learns how to bypass part of its vast formation. The meteor proves to be an Animal Kingdom trap. Jack separates from the Bromobile so Brock, Gan Salin, and Nauja can escape, then flees an early B-grade ancestor and a late B-grade Hand envoy. He enters the Animal Abyss, but Artis appears outside with Eric as a hostage. An earlier attack on Earth had been repelled by Dorman Whistles and a hidden Church elder, so Artis kidnapped Jack's five-year-old son instead. Jack exits the Abyss and submits to restraint in exchange for Eric's life. Artis kills Eric anyway. The failure to protect his child cracks Jack's Fist Dao. Jack burns through his reserves to break the envoy's domain but cannot win. Determined to survive and take revenge, he enters one of the black whirlpools roaming within the Abyss, leaving his enemies unable to follow.

Jack's connection to Brock and Boatman disappears when he enters the black hole, and both allies and enemies conclude that he died. Brock turns his grief into a campaign against Animal Kingdom slavers. Jack is actually alive inside Black Hole World, an ancient sealed refuge created by Archon Black Hole for his descendants. Mia finds and nurses him, but Eric's death and the crack in his Dao tree have reduced his power and may prevent further advancement. The peaceful inhabitants cannot leave because their space-time experts vanished long ago. Jack explores their layered world and identifies its central vortex as the true core of the Animal Abyss. The core is slowly failing, although collapse may still be far away. Jack may eventually be able to open a passage through it, but he must first repair his Dao. His family and responsibilities give him reasons to survive, while his desire for revenge remains unresolved. Outside, Brock leads the Dark Ram against Animal Kingdom operations and rescues prisoners from a slaving ship.

Jack studies grief, death, and space-time within Black Hole World. On Earth, Vivi succeeds the Professor as leader and strengthens its defenses while raising Abel. Jack realizes that his Dao failed because it did not account for those depending on his protection. He accepts his mistake, forgives himself, and repairs the cracked tree, although he channels his remaining grief into revenge. Jack learns to detach the artifact linking Black Hole World to the Animal Abyss and promises the stranded descendants that he will return when he can free them safely. Archon Black Hole's record reveals that their refuge was created during the Immortal Crusade. Jack departs with the portal artifact and emerges beside Muir Emberheart, the Animal Kingdom's middle B-grade guardian. Despite remaining C-grade, Jack kills Muir and removes the Abyss from its former location. His soul connection with Brock returns. They reunite after a year apart, and Jack explains Eric's murder, his recovery, and the hidden world. Brock, Gan Salin, Nauja, and the mobile crew commit to supporting his war against the Animal Kingdom, though they worry about the direction of his grief.

Jack's crew secretly kills Animal Kingdom enforcers, then destroys the Earthen Gemini mine. Eva Solvig confirms that Jack survived and gathers the kingdom's forces under Hand of God protection. Jack forms a Revenge fruit, while Brock warns that collective punishment would turn grief into murder. At Crown Meteor Outpost, Jack discovers human experimentation, kills its early B-grade commander, saves the prisoners, and publicly declares war on both enemy factions. The Animal Kingdom awakens two preserved founders. Meanwhile, Sovereign Heavenly Spoon leads a Black Hole Church strike team, including Min Ling and the Sage, toward the Milky Way on Boatman's orders. Jack forms a Brotherhood fruit after recognizing Brock as the person who keeps him from losing his way. A raid on Hell draws out the revived Lonahar supreme ancestor. The founder traps Jack in a prolonged late B-grade battle with twelve intelligent phantoms, but Jack imprisons the phantoms, forces a direct fight, and kills the ancestor with a final physical strike. Brock retrieves the badly injured Jack, and the Dark Ram escapes moments before Eva can stop them.

With a Church pickup approaching, Jack forms a Time fruit and attacks Animal Planet. Brock channels support from across the galaxy into him while the confrontation is broadcast. Jack kills the Animal Kingdom's entire elder corps, its remaining ancestors and founders, a Hand combatant, and Eva Solvig. Brock captures Artis, permanently seals his body, soul, and Dao, and prevents his suicide. Jack exiles Artis alive into intergalactic emptiness. Jack then tries to destroy the moon holding Emberheart civilians, but Brock blocks the attack. Gan Salin, Nauja, and the other companions join Brock, and Jack accepts that the massacre would serve his grief rather than Eric. He spares the lineage if it abandons its surname, and the survivors become Open Chest. After freeing prisoners, Jack uses an alternate teleporter route to reach Earth. He reunites with Vivi and Abel, visits his retired mother Margaret, and spends an extended month with his family through time manipulation. They bury an empty casket for Eric. When Min Ling, the Sage, Sovereign Heavenly Spoon, and the Church party arrive, Jack leaves Earth with Brock and Dorman Whistles to join the Second Crusade.

On the journey to the Black Hole Church's hidden refuge, Jack reshapes Revenge into a fruit of discipline and justice, then forms Protection as his ninth fruit. He and Brock reach peak C-grade and meet Boatman, who accepts Brock as another disciple. Leteria guides both men to a secluded asteroid, where Boatman and Elder Heavenstar oversee their public B-grade breakthroughs. Jack destroys his Dao foundation but realizes the standard nine-fruit structure lacks a final principle. He forces a tenth fruit into existence and identifies it as Freedom. Brock forms an 8,800-mile inner world, marking him as a potential future Archon. Jack's flawless ten-fruit system grows to the universe's 10,000-mile limit, making him B-grade and giving him the Paragon of Cultivation class. A heavenly tribulation immediately attacks him and changes local laws to nullify his techniques. Brock enters the storm to restore him, accepting a matching attack. Boatman intervenes to shield both disciples and weakens the tribulation. Jack destroys its final dragon and the remaining storm with Supernova, surviving the punishment for his unprecedented breakthrough.

Jack survives the heavenly tribulation as a B-grade cultivator with a 10,000-mile inner world, while Brock stands beside him with an 8,800-mile world and Boatman remains their protector. Their immediate breakthroughs end in victory, but the wider war is only expanding. Eleven returning old gods are travelling toward system space and will arrive in years. The robotic Heaven Immortal orders most forces withdrawn from system galaxies while experience gains are raised and dungeon monsters are released. The purpose is to turn widespread slaughter into a larger army. On the opposing side, an unnamed queen rallies C-grade soldiers, B-grade commanders, and A-grade generals against the immortals and their System. Her forces enter the coming conflict under the cause of freedom and justice. Jack and the weakened Black Hole Church therefore face a struggle that now reaches far beyond the defeated Animal Kingdom and the Hand of God's Milky Way branch.

characters.description: A newly advanced B-grade cultivator whose 10,000-mile inner world exceeds the accepted limit. His achievement makes him a symbol of hope for the scattered Black Hole Church and a priority target for its enemies.

characters.name: Brock

characters.name: Arch Priestess

characters.description: A Black Hole Church elder who calls Jack, Brock, and their fellow envoys together after Jack finishes stabilizing his breakthrough.
characters.name: Boatman

characters.description: Jack Rust's trusted friend and a fellow early B-grade cultivator. She promptly asks him to test their new strength in a friendly spar.
characters.name: Min Ling

characters.name: Sovereign Heavenly Spoon

characters.description: A god imprisoned within a black hole and central to the Church's long-term plans. The Church diviner explains that his own sacrifice is intended to help restore and free this captive being.

characters.name: Archon Black Hole

characters.name: the turtle guide

characters.name: the sentient stone

characters.description: A permanent duplicate formed from part of Jack's inner world and soul. It shares his memories and Dao understanding but is limited to late C-grade, and is assigned to return to Earth to protect his family.
characters.name: Jack's clone

characters.description: An E-grade djinn who manages the Church publicity campaign built around Jack and Brock. She turns their victories and cultivation progress into material intended to strengthen morale.
characters.name: Sophie

characters.name: Vivi

characters.description: The seven-year-old daughter of Jack and Vivi. She begins training at a leading Earth academy after Jack's clone returns home and settles into family life. Her education marks the beginning of her own cultivation path.
characters.name: Abel Rust

characters.description: The leader of the Immortals and principal authority at the summit forced upon the Black Hole Church. The remote meeting places this System-aligned enemy at the center of the campaign against the Church.
characters.name: Heaven Immortal

characters.description: A peak B-grade Black Hole Church ally with distinctive star-like hair who accompanies Jack Rust's party.
characters.name: Spacewind

characters.name: Great Silver

characters.name: Saturnstar

characters.description: An early B-grade soldier in the Black Hole Church's Featherwell Battalion. Inspired by Brock's example, he holds a threatened battle line and risks himself to save a fellow soldier.
characters.name: Centrum Night Sky

description.text: The sixth entry in the series opens with the Black Hole Church scattered and in retreat after losing its stronghold, its remaining forces hunted across a systemless galaxy. When news breaks that Jack Rust and his companion Brock have each achieved unprecedented cultivation breakthroughs, the Church's leadership publicizes their success to rally flagging morale, instantly making the pair priority targets for the ruling immortals. Brought to the Church's new headquarters under the personal patronage of its leader, the Arch Priestess, Jack works to stabilize his unusual foundation and finds a way to maintain contact with his family on Earth even as his war against the immortals draws him further from home.

recaps.ending: Jack defeats the hostile life god in the dimensional sea after Brock lends him temporary S-grade power. The victory also destroys the other gods absorbed by the life god, while the Heaven Immortal has already been killed. Boatman and the Arch Priestess die during the final defense, but Jack, Brock, Min Ling, Sovereign Heavenly Spoon, Fiend Prince, Great Silver, Vivi, Abel, and Jack's Earth clone survive. Fifty years later, Jack has judged the surrendered Immortal forces without punishing innocent relatives, removed rewards for killing from the rebuilt System, and reorganized the Bare Fist Brotherhood around justice and reconstruction. The surviving entropy, space, and time god clones train later generations in the Space Monster World under the Hall's continuing protection. Black Hole World and Green Dragon Realm have joined the main universe. Jack is now a late A-grade and the strongest person in the universe, but true S-grade remains ahead. He and Brock pioneer new galaxies while postponing exploration of the dimensional sea. On Earth, the clone lives with Vivi and receives visits from the adult Abel. Margaret Rust died ten years after the war and was not revived.
recaps.in_short: Jack Rust and Brock become exceptional B-grades and public champions of the Black Hole Church, then enter the Space Monster World seeking the power needed for Jack's duel with Elder Hero. They survive the Hall of Trials, kill Fiend King, and reach A-grade through unconventional foundations. Jack returns with Great Silver's army, defeats Hero, and helps launch the final war. The released life god destroys the Heaven Immortal but reveals its plan to eliminate all other life. Boatman and the Arch Priestess die protecting the Church, while Brock channels the survivors' resolve into temporary S-grade power for Jack. Jack destroys the god and ends the war. Fifty years later, he has reformed the System, judged the surrendered Immortal forces, and become the universe's strongest person while pioneering new galaxies with Brock. Vivi, Jack's clone, and their adult daughter Abel remain on Earth.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Rust is an Earth cultivator whose path is inseparable from Brock, his spiritually linked brorilla brother. Their bond has made them partners in cultivation and conflict rather than master and subordinate. Jack's closest family remains on Earth. Vivi Aragon is his partner and has succeeded Margaret Rust, known as the Professor, as the planet's leader. Their daughter Abel Rust is growing up under Vivi's care, while Margaret has retired from leadership. Jack's responsibilities therefore extend beyond his personal advancement to Earth, his family, Brock, and the wider struggle surrounding the Black Hole Church. These established bonds and obligations shape the choices he carries into the new volume.

The Black Hole Church is losing hidden positions when news arrives that Jack has formed a 10,000-mile B-grade inner world and Brock an 8,800-mile one. The Arch Priestess turns their achievements into symbols of resistance, prompting the Immortals to place a major bounty on them. Boatman sends the pair toward the new Cathedral and assigns a weaker soul clone to escort them. Along the way, Jack learns that ordinary cultivation is far too slow for his enormous foundation and that the Church diviner carries a fragment of the imprisoned life god. The journey includes a staged fight against an A-grade space monster, after which the turtle within Jack's life drop awakens and identifies itself as Archon Black Hole's former companion. At the Cathedral, the Arch Priestess offers Jack and Brock extensive resources in exchange for serving as public champions. She also proposes a permanent soul-linked clone so Jack can receive System-dependent Dao visions and maintain a presence with his family on Earth.

Jack creates a permanent late C-grade clone and sends it toward Earth while his main body remains with the Church. Core absorption advances Jack only slowly, but the clone retrieves the dragon Archon's hidden realm, settles its divided inhabitants, and permanently joins it to Jack's inner world. Jack also connects Black Hole World, gaining stability and life energy from the two dimensions. Brock defeats the hostile Church envoy in a highly publicized duel, and their former feud ends in mutual acceptance. Jack's clone briefly enters System space and receives a Dao vision showing that death energy can arise from compressed space near a black hole. Jack's first experiment with the principle nearly destroys his arms but advances his understanding. The clone then reaches Earth and reunites with Vivi and seven-year-old Abel. Vivi now leads the planet, while the clone settles into family life and supports Abel's training. Meanwhile, Brock reveals that the Arch Priestess is a space monster and that they have become partners.

The Immortals expose and ambush several hidden Church battalions, then force the Arch Priestess to swear that she will attend a summit. She satisfies the oath safely by using Jack's Immortal Commune ability as a remote link. At the summit, the Immortals seek the neutrality of the Space Monster World. Jack instead accepts a death duel with their early A-grade champion, with a future alliance and the Arch Priestess's freedom among the stakes. After reaching middle B-grade, Jack decides that the sealed Space Monster World offers his best chance to gather the resources needed to win. He leaves with Brock, Spacewind, and protective clones of Boatman and the Arch Priestess. An enemy Archon intercepts them at the portal. Both protective clones are destroyed while delaying the attacker. Spacewind sacrifices half of his star-powered hair, Brock overextends himself, and Jack activates the ship's concealed weapon. The three survivors cross the seal alive, but enter the hostile world without their intended protectors.

Inside the Space Monster World, Jack and Spacewind disguise themselves as local Double Devils while Brock travels openly. The group learns the world's provincial structure and reaches Empty Star City before a major auction. Jack publicly challenges Saturnstar, a peak B-grade disciple, and kills him, gaining enough wealth to bid on a damaged manual concerning space, death, and black holes. He secures the manual by manipulating a hostile A-grade elder into wasting resources on other lots. Its surviving teachings show Jack how to create an artificial black-hole effect, though his first attempts remain unstable. Jack also accepts conditional entry into the Great Silver Faction for a future Dark Canal expedition. When the group leaves after six months, the hostile elder pursues them. Jack fights rather than flee. His usual techniques and temporary life-drop battle form cannot finish the A-grade opponent, so he deliberately accepts severe injury to charge his experimental attack. The space-and-death singularity destroys the elder's torso, giving Jack his first A-grade kill.

The slain elder's ring contains an Overlord core and other valuable resources. Jack spends almost four years absorbing the core without dilution, repeatedly destroying and rebuilding his body until he reaches late B-grade and gains much greater density and control of his mass. Brock reaches late B-grade, and Spacewind recovers much of the cultivation lost during their escape. Although they miss Great Silver's deadline, they earn places in the Dark Canal Delve by defeating three faction qualifiers. Great Silver recognizes Jack as human but spares him, judging the Immortals the greater danger. During the delve, two rival escort leaders abandon their duty to seize a Golden Earth Lotus guarded by a powerful elemental. After the guardian falls, Jack kills both exhausted leaders, surviving a will-based duel with the second. Brock prevents the disciples from interfering and defeats their strongest members without killing them. With the elders dead, Jack and Brock control the treasure site and become the effective protectors of the surviving disciples.

Brock absorbs the Golden Earth Lotus and its guardian's core, reaching the peak of B-grade, while Jack distributes the remaining resources and leads the survivors to the Hall of Trials. Elsewhere, eleven old gods enter the Second Crusade and briefly reverse the Church's battlefield losses. In the Hall, Jack and Brock undertake tests of Dao understanding, willpower, and combat. Both receive the highest classification in the first two tests. Jack's final opponent is a mortal fragment of the entropy god whose Dao can decay body, soul, and lifespan. Jack wins by forcing entropy into an unstable Black Hole, causing the technique to expand beyond the fragment's control. The defeated fragment explains that divided gods created the Space Monster World, its peoples, and the Hall to train soldiers against the maker of the ancients. Jack and Brock earn Eternal results in all three categories and qualify for a hidden seventh floor. They learn that Great Silver and Fiend King are forcibly opening a route to that severed inheritance, and decide to follow.

The Hall exposes Jack's true identity to the monster disciples before he and Brock reach the severed seventh floor. They discover Fiend King looting it and betraying Great Silver during a confrontation with the Stone Scholar, the guardian who created Jack's sentient stone. Jack and Brock reveal themselves, combine their spiritually linked combat, and kill Fiend King. They then claim separate Dao and cultivation inheritances. Brock reaches A-grade first. Jack rejects the standard route after deciding that creating life in a separate inner world does not fit his path. Instead, he fuses his body, Dao, fist, and inner world into a universe of the body, embedding his connected realms within himself and reaching A-grade beyond the System's normal progression. After roughly ten years of seclusion, Jack and Brock leave with the Hall's manuals and Frankie, another sentient stone. Great Silver accepts Jack's power and commits the Space Monster World to the coming war. The Stone Scholar remains as the Hall's guardian, and Fiend Prince becomes Jack's first disciple.

Jack and Brock return to the Church after fifteen years with Great Silver and a compact monster army. The old gods have already fought the Immortals and lost one of their number, while the remaining alliance distrusts what the gods may do after victory. The Church plans to use Jack's accelerated duel with Elder Hero to gather every major force while the Sage secretly attempts to free the imprisoned life god. Before battle, Church fighters remove their System mini-cores, and Jack permanently destroys his own. Jack dominates Hero until the Immortal champion burns the dead god of mass's core. Jack undermines the belief-based Dao supporting Hero, extracts the borrowed core, and leaves a concealed Black Hole inside him. Hero dies after the Heaven Immortal retrieves him. The armies converge, but the gods detect the covert rescue and teleport the battlefield to the prison. The entropy god destroys the ritual columns, leaving the life god trapped while open war begins around the black hole.

Jack kills Archon Three Lives and helps the Church's younger fighters survive the main battle. The gods combine into stronger forms, but the Heaven Immortal recalls the System mini-cores from its army and absorbs their accumulated power, becoming stronger than the divine alliance. With defeat imminent, the entropy god begins dissolving the black hole to release the life god. Church leaders sacrifice themselves to hold back the Heaven Immortal. Boatman dies after entrusting his scythe to Jack. The life god emerges, enters the Sage's body, absorbs the remaining gods, and reaches S-grade. It destroys the Heaven Immortal, then reveals that the rescue was part of its own plan. Rather than protect the Church, it intends to eliminate all other life as a possible threat. The god massacres cultivators, restrains the survivors, and attacks Jack through Copy Jack. The Sage is revealed as its avatar, while Copy Jack was its hidden route into Jack's soul. Jack resists the attempt to erase his identity but remains trapped.

Jack's resistance forces the life god to pause its soul attack. Brock then turns the Church's shared resolve into Brotherhood and channels the combined power into Jack. The Arch Priestess dies blocking the god's attempt to stop the transfer. With temporary S-grade strength, Jack takes the god into the dimensional sea to protect the survivors. He destroys the compromised life drop, overcomes the god's attempt to force destructive evolution through his body, and finally understands the universe-creation vision that had long eluded him. A newborn world and a destructive black hole combine into the attack that kills the life god and the gods it absorbed. Jack survives and returns to his normal power. Fifty years later, the surrendered Immortal forces have been judged individually. Jack has removed killing rewards from the rebuilt System and leads reconstruction through the Bare Fist Brotherhood. The surviving god clones train new generations in the Space Monster World. Jack is the universe's strongest person and pioneers new galaxies with Brock, while Vivi, Jack's clone, and adult Abel remain on Earth.
